experiment.title: You're approving the wrong things
experiment.hook: reversible. ambiguous. irreversible. only one should reach you.
experiment.hypothesis: a 'you're doing X wrong' mistake-callout hook plus a single reframe line ('scale review with consequence, not activity') beats a framework list for cold reach
experiment.caption:
hit a point a few weeks ago where I was drowning in approve/deny prompts from my own agents and realized I'd basically rebuilt the exact job I was trying to get rid of. like every single step wanted a thumbs up. and most of them did not matter at all, renaming a file, drafting a doc, whatever. but buried in there was the one that could actually message a client or merge into main. so it clicked, I don't need to review activity, I need to review consequence. reversible + cheap, let it run. irreversible or ambiguous, that's mine, and everything else is just policy: publishing, payments, outbound messages, merges gate at the human boundary and an unknown high-risk tool fails closed instead of guessing. autonomy is useful but it's worthless if I'm still the bottleneck on every keystroke. still tuning exactly where the line sits but

slides.headline: reversible. ambiguous. irreversible. only one should reach you.
slides.subtext: you're the bottleneck you were trying to delete.

slides.headline: 50 notifications. 49 are noise. 1 could publish to prod.
approve everything and you do the work. approve nothing and it ships blind.
human review should scale with consequence, not activity
slides.subtext: reserve your attention for what can't be undone.

slides.headline: reversible + low-stakes runs. irreversible + ambiguous stops.
publishing, payments, messages, merges gate at the human boundary
slides.subtext: an unknown high-risk tool fails closed. every time.

slides.headline: what did you approve today that a policy could've handled?
slides.subtext: consequence-based escalation lives in OrgX. follow for the systems.
